retrievedClauses.text: 4. Flammable and explosive materials: such materials must be stored separately in dedicated stores away from ignition and heat sources, with ventilation, explosion-proof, lightning-protection and anti-static provisions; incompatible materials must never be co-stored.

1. Evacuation routes and exits: evacuation routes and emergency exits must be kept clear at all times; occupying, blocking or sealing them is strictly prohibited. Exit doors must open in the direction of travel and must not be fitted with thresholds or screens. [Fire Protection Law of the PRC (《中华人民共和国消防法》), Art. 28]
9. Fire service access: fire lanes and fire-service access areas must never be occupied, blocked or obstructed, and must maintain the required clear width and height.
5. Fire control room: must be staffed 24 hours a day by certified operators, with complete duty logs and equipment in normal working order.
7. Emergency lighting and exit signage: exit signs and emergency lighting must be intact, correctly oriented, unobstructed and functional on power loss.

2. Fire extinguishers: extinguishers must be provided and maintained per GB 50140 Code for design of extinguisher distribution in buildings (《建筑灭火器配置设计规范》). Pressure gauges and expiry dates must be checked periodically; units must not be removed, obstructed or corroded.

scene: A storage area adjacent to a stainless steel door, with various materials and tools stored on both sides.
description: The image shows a narrow passageway or storage space flanked by shelves and construction materials. On the left side, long pipes and rods are leaning against the wall, some wrapped in plastic. A red broom or mop is visible near the center-left. To the right, metal shelving holds boxes, bags, and other supplies, including what appears to be electrical components and packaging materials. The central feature is a closed stainless steel door with decorative patterns, likely an exit or access point. The area appears cluttered, with items stored close to the door and along the pathway.

findings.evidence: Construction materials (pipes, brooms) are stored directly beside and partially obstructing the doorway, reducing clearance.
findings.explanation: The presence of stored items near the door impedes quick egress during an emergency. In case of fire, this obstruction could delay evacuation and hinder firefighter access.
findings.regulation: Fire Protection Law of the PRC (《中华人民共和国消防法》), Art. 28

findings.evidence: Shelving and stored goods extend into the corridor, narrowing the passage width.
findings.explanation: Narrowed pathways reduce the ability of personnel or equipment to move quickly through the area, especially during emergencies. This may also prevent proper deployment of firefighting tools.
findings.regulation: Fire Protection Law of the PRC (《中华人民共和国消防法》), Art. 28

findings.evidence: Plastic-wrapped materials and cardboard boxes are stored in close proximity to the door and in confined spaces.
findings.explanation: Plastic and cardboard are combustible materials; when stored densely in enclosed areas, they can contribute to rapid fire spread if ignited. Lack of ventilation and separation increases risk.
findings.regulation: Fire Protection Law of the PRC (《中华人民共和国消防法》), Art. 28

verdict: The scene contains multiple fire hazards, primarily due to blocked exits and improper storage of combustible materials.
suggestions: Clear all items from within 1 meter of the door to ensure unobstructed access and egress.
Relocate flammable materials such as plastic-wrapped items and cardboard boxes to designated storage areas away from doors and corridors.
Ensure that all evacuation routes remain clear at all times and conduct regular inspections.
